THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA
ORAL JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the owner of the bus has challenged the liability fastened against him as per the judgment and award dated 20.01.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.100/2012 by the Court of Senior Civil Judge and Addl.MACT., Harihar ('the Tribunal' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
3. Undisputedly, there was an accident on 09.12.2011 at about 5.00 p.m. near Adapoora village cross on Davanagere-Malebennur Road involving a bus bearing No.KA-17/B-149.

Due to capsize of the bus, NC: 2024:KHC:32936 several inmates of the bus have sustained injuries and the Insurance Company has satisfied the award in respect of injured passengers and several cases are said to be settled in Lok Adalat.
In respect of one Anjini @ Anjaneya, the claim is made by his wife, son and parents.

The Tribunal considering the material on record assessed compensation of Rs.9,91,000/-
and directed the owner of the bus to pay with interest @ 6% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the same, the owner of the bus has filed this appeal on various heads.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.R.Gopal, learned counsel for the owner, Ms.S.P.Shruthi, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.O.Mahesh, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the owner of the bus that the deceased was not the cleaner, he was not appointed as the cleaner, he was only a passenger, policy of insurance covers the risk of 48 NC: 2024:KHC:32936 passengers and 2 employees.

Among the injured passengers,
Sri Manoharsa N Ladwa vs Smt. Rajamma @ Rajeshwari on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195149733/
3 deceased was also a passenger.

sentences.text: Even if the deceased was considered as an employee, policy of insurance covers the risk of two employees and in the accident, only one employee has been injured and succumbed to death, the Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation.

5.1. It is his strenuous contention that either deceased must be treated as a regular passenger or one of the employees as the cover note did not point out specifically that the employee shall only be a driver or conductor.

It is the duty on the part of the Insurance Company to produce the policy of insurance, same is not produced and before the Tribunal, specific plea is taken that the deceased was not a cleaner and he was a passenger, but erroneous finding is recorded by the Tribunal.

5.2. It is further contended that during the pendency of the appeal, owner has died and his legal NC:
2024:KHC:32936 representatives are brought on record.
They have not succeeded to any of the estate of the owner and they cannot be made liable to pay compensation personally.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the prosecution papers from the first inception of setting the law into motion i.e., filing of the complaint by a passenger of the bus point out that the deceased was not a passenger of the bus.
The petitioners claim that the deceased was a cleaner under the owner in the said bus.
Evidence was let in and the prosecution of the driver of the bus was also under Section 304A of IPC on the ground that his actionable negligence caused the death of cleaner of the bus.

6.1. Learned counsel also brought to the notice of the court, the admission made by the owner of the bus in the course of cross-examination that he has obtained the insurance cover only to the driver and conductor of the bus.
In the evidence there is no reference from the owner that the insurance cover is taken for cleaner.
Contrary to the material on record, the owner to avoid his liability contends that the deceased was not the cleaner.
The Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence and fastened the liability against the owner and Insurance Company is rightly exonerated and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the compensation awarded is on the lower side including the conventional heads.
She sought indulgence of the court to enhance the compensation suo motu.

Either the Insurance Company or the owner, whoever is responsible, shall pay the compensation at the earliest as the petitioners being the victims of the accident are waiting to enjoy the fruits of the award.
8. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
9. The only dispute is, whether the deceased was a cleaner or a passenger of the bus.

Ex.P2 is the complaint NC: 2024:KHC:32936 filed by one Nazarulla, the passenger of the bus, who set the law into motion on 09.12.2011 at 5.00 p.m. that in the accident, cleaner of the bus died at the spot with specific reference to Anjani.

It is interesting to note that the owner of the bus has got released the Sri Manoharsa N Ladwa vs Smt. Rajamma @ Rajeshwari on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195149733/
4 vehicle by executing an indemnity bond.

sentences.text: In the indemnity bond, there is a specific plea that the cleaner of the said bus 'Anjani' was died.
During the course of cross- examination, the owner of the vehicle has clearly stated that the insurance cover obtained for 48 passengers and two employees.
These two employees have been elicited on behalf of the Insurance Company that one was the driver and another was the conductor.
The owner of the bus did not assert that the insurance was obtained for employees irrespective of the driver, conductor or the cleaner.
10. The inquest panchanama too confirmed that the deceased was working as a cleaner.
In the claim petition, the petitioners specifically asserted that the deceased was a cleaner in the bus.
The cross- NC: 2024:KHC:32936 examination of the witnesses on behalf of the petitioners stands and asserted that the deceased was a cleaner.
The owner of the bus was expecting the petitioners to prove that the deceased was the cleaner.

At an undisputed point of time, a person who is not interested in the claim, makes a specific statement that the deceased Anjani was a cleaner, who are the persons seen the deceased working as a cleaner in the bus soon before the accident.

Before the Tribunal, the owner gives a statement that the policy of insurance covers the risk of driver and the conductor,
while getting the bus released executes indemnity bond stating that its cleaner Anjani died in the accident.

The prosecution papers stand in support of the petitioners that the deceased was a cleaner of the bus and there is no satisfactory explanation from the owner of the bus that he has not engaged the services of deceased as a cleaner.
Under these circumstances, there is no reason to find any error or illegality in the finding recorded by the Tribunal.
As regards liability on the part of the Insurance Company to indemnify, the claim against the cleaner, the policy of insurance is not made available.
Only the cover note is made available as per Ex.R1.
Even the premium paid on the cover note through cheque came to be dishonoured and it is submitted that later premium amount was paid in cash.
In the cover note, the licenced carrying capacity is mentioned as '48' passengers, driver and other two, with total of '50'.
The Insurance Company is ready to compensate in respect of the deceased provided it is proved that he is a passenger.

Contrarily, the material on record points out that the deceased was a cleaner and the owner himself admits in the witness box on oath that the policy covers the risk of the driver and the conductor only.
Under such circumstances, it is hard to accept the contentions urged on behalf of the owner of the bus.

12. Adverting to the submission made by Sri.R.Gopal, learned counsel for the legal representatives of the original owner that they are not succeeded to any - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:32936 estate of the deceased, it is a matter to be urged in the execution proceedings and not at this stage.

In this background, there is no merit in the appeal, in the result, the following;
Sri Manoharsa N Ladwa vs Smt. Rajamma @ Rajeshwari
